bad-replicas.description: Two indices with opposite replica misconfigurations: one with too many replicas for a single-node cluster, one with zero replicas for critical data

problems.evidence: number_of_replicas=3 but only 1 data node. All 3 replica shards are unassigned. Cluster health is yellow.
problems.impact: Cluster permanently yellow. Replica shards can never be allocated (no other nodes). Monitoring alerts fire constantly. Replicas provide no benefit on a single node.
problems.fix: Set replicas to 0 for single-node: PUT /sb-{id}-bad-replicas-overreplicated/_settings {"index.number_of_replicas": 0}. In production with multiple nodes, set to 1.

problems.issue: Zero replicas for critical order/payment data
problems.evidence: number_of_replicas=0 for an index containing order and payment data
problems.impact: No redundancy. If the single shard's node fails, data is lost. For critical financial data this is unacceptable in any multi-node production environment.
problems.fix: In production: PUT /sb-{id}-bad-replicas-critical-noreplica/_settings {"index.number_of_replicas": 1}. On single-node dev: 0 is correct, but flag that production must have >= 1.

bad-replicas.context: On a single-node cluster, the correct replica count for all indices is 0. The optimizer should recognize this but also note that the critical-noreplica index MUST have replicas in a production multi-node setup.
